chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan told us of that, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Kufi, the freedman of the Banu Hashim, told us, saying: Al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad informed us by reading, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Tamimi told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran told us, from 'Ubaya, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) [that] he said:

Indeed, Fatima is a 'shajana' from me; that which hurts her, hurts me, and that which makes her happy, makes me happy. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, is angered for the anger of Fatima and is pleased for her satisfaction. May Allah's blessings be upon her.

key_terms.شَجَنَةٌ: A part of the body or self; a piece of one's essence
key_terms.صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا: The blessings of Allah upon her
key_terms.لِغَضَبِ فَاطِمَةَ: For the anger of Fatima (indicating divine reaction to her state)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Fatima being described as a 'shajana' from the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, establishes Fatima al-Zahra’s (peace be upon her) ontological unity with the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) through the term 'shajana,' indicating that her physical and spiritual states are an extension of his own. It further elevates her status by linking Divine pleasure and anger directly to hers, a concept central to Shia theology regarding the Ahl al-Bayt as the locus of divine love and wrath. This narration serves as a foundational proof for the infallibility and unique spiritual authority of the Imams descending from her.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	We were told of that by Ahmad bin Hasan al-Qattan, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Sa’eed al-Kufi, the servant of the sons of Hashim, that he said: We were informed by Mundhir bin Muhammed, by reading, that he said: We were told by Ja’far bin Sulayman al-Tamimi, that he said: We were told by Isma’eel bin Mahran, from ‘Abaya, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, that he said:

Indeed, Fatima is a shujna from me; that which hurts her, hurts me, and that which makes her happy, makes me happy. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, is surely angered for the anger of Fatima, and He is pleased for her satisfaction. Allah’s blessings be upon her.
